questions.q: What does this lesson say actually turns a deployment script into real, trustworthy automation?
options: Checking whether the deployment failed and alerting a human, rather than the deployment command itself
Running the deployment command manually every single time
Deleting the database and recreating it from scratch on every deploy
Removing all error handling to keep the script simple
questions.explain: The deployment command is one line and already covered in Lessons 66-67; the alert-on-failure logic is what makes it operational.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what should a DBA check first when an automated deployment fails?
options: The pipeline log — the database itself is often untouched and fine
Immediately restore the database from the most recent backup
Immediately rebuild every index in the database
Assume the T-SQL inside the deployed change is always the cause
questions.explain: The lesson stresses that pipeline failures are frequently about the pipeline's own plumbing (auth, parameters), not the database.

questions.q: Why do permission errors show up in automated pipelines that never happen when a DBA runs the same command manually?
options: Because the pipeline authenticates as a service principal or managed identity with narrower rights than the DBA's own login
Because pipelines always run with full administrator rights
Because manual commands bypass Azure security entirely
Because pipelines use a different SQL dialect than manual commands
questions.explain: The identity a pipeline runs as is distinct from and typically narrower than a DBA's personal login.

questions.q: What technique does this lesson recommend to isolate whether a failure is the pipeline's environment or the deployment itself?
options: Re-run the exact same command manually with identical parameters
Change the parameters randomly until it works
Delete the pipeline and never automate that task again
Contact Microsoft support before checking anything locally
questions.explain: If the manual run with identical parameters succeeds, the pipeline's environment — not the template — is the likely culprit.

questions.q: Which course and lessons does this lesson point to for a deeper, dedicated CI/CD pipeline build (merge triggers, tests, secrets management)?
options: Git/GitHub & CI/CD for Data, Lessons 22 and 23
Terraform & Bicep for Data Engineers, Lesson 20
T-SQL Development, Lesson 60
This same course's Lesson 60
questions.explain: Lesson 22 (Deploying on Merge to Main) and Lesson 23 (Environment Variables & Secrets in CI/CD) in Git/GitHub & CI/CD for Data cover that ground in full.
